items.quote: Microstructures and equilibrium phase compositions were investigated using a LEO-1450 SEM (Zeiss, Germany) equipped with NORAN7 EDS (Thermo Scientific, America).

items.label: ternary alloy samples
items.quote: Pure elements of granular iron (99.99 wt.%), lump nickel (99.99 wt.%) and lump tantalum (99.99 wt.%), supplied by China New Metal Materials Technology Co., Ltd., were used as starting materials in the present work. All ternary alloy samples were prepared from pure elements using an arc-melting on a water-cooled copper hearth under highpurity Ar atmosphere.
items.starting_materials: granular iron (99.99 wt.%), lump nickel (99.99 wt.%) and lump tantalum (99.99 wt.%)
items.synthesis: arc-melting on a water-cooled copper hearth under highpurity Ar atmosphere

items.applies_to: as-cast samples with a mass of 4 g
items.atmosphere_or_container: sealed in quartz tubes under a vacuum of 6 9 10-2 Pa
items.purpose: to retain the microstructure prevalent at high temperature
items.quote: The other as-cast samples with a mass of 4 g were sealed in quartz tubes under a vacuum of 6 9 10-2 Pa and annealed in chamber furnaces (MTI KSL1400 and MTI KSL-1200) at 1200  C for 30 days and 1000  C for 50 days, respectively. At the end of the heat treatment, the sample capsules were quenched in water to retain the microstructure prevalent at high temperature.

items.applies_to: as-cast samples with a mass of 4 g
items.atmosphere_or_container: sealed in quartz tubes under a vacuum of 6 9 10-2 Pa
items.purpose: to retain the microstructure prevalent at high temperature
items.quote: The other as-cast samples with a mass of 4 g were sealed in quartz tubes under a vacuum of 6 9 10-2 Pa and annealed in chamber furnaces (MTI KSL1400 and MTI KSL-1200) at 1200  C for 30 days and 1000  C for 50 days, respectively. At the end of the heat treatment, the sample capsules were quenched in water to retain the microstructure prevalent at high temperature.
EDX spectra acquired from large sample areas were used to quantify the integral chemical composition of the samples.
Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy dispersive xray analysis (EDX) were carried out in a SEM type Gemini 1550.
XRD-measurements were carried out in a DRON-3 diffractometer on powdered samples using Cu Ka radiation.

items.applies_to: all samples in the as-cast condition
items.quote: Microsegregation was analyzed for all samples in the as-cast condition, using the EDX grid measurement technique [29,30].

items.calibration: W/W-20Re string thermocouple designed by Kocherzhinskiy et al. [31,32]
items.crucible: Sc2O3 and Al2O3 crucibles (the latter for sample no. 1, only)
items.quote: Temperatures of solid-state and solid-liquid phase transformations were determined by DTA using Sc2O3 and Al2O3 crucibles (the latter for sample no. 1, only) and W/W-20Re string thermocouple designed by Kocherzhinskiy et al. [31,32].

items.calibration: IPTS-90 reference points of Al, Au, Pd, Pt, Rh and additional reference points of Fe and Al2O3
items.quote: The thermocouple was calibrated using the IPTS-90 reference points of Al, Au, Pd, Pt, Rh and additional reference points of Fe and Al2O3.

items.label: 7 samples
items.quote: A number of 7 samples with different chemical composition were prepared by arc melting, each with a mass of 15 g.

items.label: sample no. 4
items.quote: The sample no. 4 with the integral chemical composition Fe45.1 at.%Ta displays a two-phase microstructure consisting of l þ m.

items.label: sample no. 1
items.quote: In the alloys Fe-15.6 at.% Ta (sample no. 1) and Fe-64.2 at.% Ta (sample no. 7) the eutectic microstructure formed after solidification of the primary phase is displayed in Fig. 2, resulting from the reactions L 4 l þ (dFe) and L 4 m þ b, respectively.

items.label: sample no. 7
items.quote: In the alloys Fe-15.6 at.% Ta (sample no. 1) and Fe-64.2 at.% Ta (sample no. 7) the eutectic microstructure formed after solidification of the primary phase is displayed in Fig. 2, resulting from the reactions L 4 l þ (dFe) and L 4 m þ b, respectively.
Otherwise microsegregation in samples no. 4 (Fe-45.2 at.% Ta) and no. 5 (Fe-52.3 at.% Ta) should display a decreasing Ta-content.

The measured microsegregation profiles show that in samples no. 1 (Fe-15.6 at.% Ta) and no. 2 (Fe32.2 at.% Ta) the Ta-content decreases as solidification proceeds, whereas all other samples show the opposite behaviour.
In samples no. 4 (Fe-45.1 at.%Ta), no. 5 (Fe-45.2 at.% Ta) and no. 6 (Fe-56.2 at.% Ta) minor amounts of an unknown phase were detected, composition of which is close a Ta3Fe2 stoichiometry.

Fig. 3. Samples containing small amounts of a Ta-rich phase (bright particles), possibly the metastable Ta3Fe2 phase, that persists even after annealing at 1973 K for 5 h (a) alloy Fe45.1 at.% Ta and (b) alloy Fe-52.3 at.% Ta.
